positions.notes: Stage 1 translator: en «Discover the oasis» / ar «اكتشف الواحة». 探索 + 绿洲 (termbase and TM: 绿洲 is the fixed rendering of «الواحة»; the old nav.discover is already 探索, so the group title extends a published word). Stage 2 editor: verb-object heading of four characters, the usual rhythm of Chinese destination menus. 发现绿洲 rejected: 发现 reads as a one-off find, 探索 is the travel-site idiom for browsing. 游览绿洲 rejected: it narrows the group to sightseeing, yet the group also holds trails, map, events and leisure. 绿洲探索 rejected as stiffer noun inversion. Stage 3 localizer: no 您, no exclamation; neutral for a mainland traveller. Stage 4 benchmarker: official portals use 探索 + place name for the top menu (探索某地); no proper name involved. Stage 5 proofreader: simplified only, no punctuation, no Latin; width margin +210px, four characters is far shorter than the English reference.

Stage 1 translator: en «Taste and shop» / ar «تذوّق وتسوّق». The group holds food (哈萨美食), dining (餐厅与咖啡馆), fruits (绿洲水果) and online stores (网店), so the title must cover buying as well as eating. 美食与购物 = two nouns joined by 与, the pattern already used in the bar («餐厅与咖啡馆», «传统集市、公园与农场»). Stage 2 editor: 品尝与选购 and 品味与选购 rejected: verb pair clashes with the noun-style labels beneath and 品味 drifts to «taste/refinement». 吃喝与购物 rejected as colloquial. The Arabic wordplay is not carried, meaning only (per brief). Stage 3 localizer: 美食 and 购物 are the two interests Chinese travellers look for first; 购物 here names a section of the menu, and the stores label itself stays 网店 (earlier decision, nav-stores). Stage 4 benchmarker: VisitSaudi zh uses 购物 and 美食 as section names; 美食 is also the termbase choice in 哈萨美食. Stage 5 proofreader: simplified only, no punctuation, no Latin; width margin +210px, five characters, passes.

Stage 1 translator: en «Arrange your visit» / ar «رتّب زيارتك». Contents: 住宿 · 地图 · 我的收藏, i.e. practical preparation. Stage 2 editor: 出行准备 is a nominal heading of the same size as 探索绿洲 and 美食与购物 (one consistent form: short heading phrase, no pronoun, no 您, no imperative particle). Stage 3 localizer: distinct from the gold button 行程规划 (nav.plan): the button means itinerary planning, this title means getting ready to travel, so the two do not duplicate or approximate each other. Rejected: 安排行程 and 规划行程 (same words as 行程规划, would repeat the button), 安排您的游程 (pronoun, and near-duplicate), 行程准备 (contains 行程, too close to the button), 出行指南 (promises a guide page that the group does not hold), 游览安排 (near-duplicate of the button). Stage 4 benchmarker: 出行准备 is the common portal heading for accommodation, maps and saved items; no proper name. This title appears in the menu only (the bar shows its links flat, name kept for screen readers), so the bar budget is untouched. Stage 5 proofreader: simplified only, no punctuation, no Latin.

Stage 1 translator: en «Change» / ar «تغيير». The row reads «语言：简体中文 …… 切换 ⌄» and opens the language list. 切换 is the standard Chinese UI verb for switching language or account (切换语言). Stage 2 editor: 更改 and 更换 rejected: they say «alter/replace a setting», 切换 says «switch between options», which is what the dropdown does; 变更 too formal. Stage 3 localizer: two characters, matches the short button verbs of the zh block (关闭, 阅读中文版). Stage 4 benchmarker: mainland apps and sites use 切换 beside the current language name. Termbase: no entry; TM: no conflicting pair; lang.menu is 语言 already, so no repetition of the noun. Stage 5 proofreader: simplified only, no punctuation, no Latin.
